office.title: Indiana School Board Member
office.summary: A school board is the elected or appointed governing body of a public school corporation, the legal unit that runs a local school district [1, 2]. The board hires and evaluates the superintendent, adopts policies, and approves the annual budget, while the superintendent and staff run schools day to day [3]. Most boards have five or seven members serving staggered four-year terms [3]. Starting in 2026, candidates may list a political party, run as independents, or list no affiliation on the ballot, and there is no primary for these seats [2, 4].

facts.label: Term
facts.value: 4 years, with elections staggered so part of the board is chosen every two years [3]

facts.label: Elected
facts.value: At the November general election (November 3, 2026, or November 2028 for some seats); depending on the local organization plan, members represent the whole school corporation (at large) or a district within it, and some boards are wholly or partly appointed [2]

facts.label: Ballot label
facts.value: Each candidate chooses a party label, 'Independent', or no affiliation, shown next to the name; no primary and no straight-ticket voting for these races [2, 4]

facts.label: Pay
facts.value: Set by board resolution: an annual amount of no more than 10% of the lowest starting teacher salary in the school corporation, plus a capped per diem [5]

duties: Hires, evaluates and can dismiss the superintendent, and approves the hiring and firing of principals, teachers and other staff recommended by the superintendent [1, 7, 3].
Adopts the annual budget, appropriates funds and oversees school finances [1, 3].

Decides whether to ask voters to approve an operating referendum (an extra property tax levy); the board adopts the resolution and the Department of Local Government Finance reviews the ballot language for compliance with state law [8].
Approves contracts, buys and sells property, and decides on construction, repair and demolition of school buildings [1].

Bargains with the teachers' union over salary, wages and wage-related benefits such as health insurance and retirement; state law excludes teacher evaluation procedures from those bargaining subjects [9].
Writes and updates policies and rules for schools, often in a policy handbook, including the student handbook [1, 3].
Buys curricular materials, provides them to students without charge, and runs programs such as student transportation and school lunch [1].

Must adopt a process for parents and residents to ask that library material be removed as obscene or harmful to minors, review requests at public meetings and keep a public catalog of library materials [10].
Hears written appeals of student expulsions, unless the board has voted not to hear them [11].
Must take official action openly; Indiana's Open Door Law says public agencies' official action is to be conducted openly so the people may be fully informed [12, 13].

A school board member must have lived in the school corporation (and, for a district seat, the district) for at least one year before the election, and a teacher or other employee of the school corporation may not serve on its board [2].

What the board does not control: the State Board of Education adopts statewide academic standards [14], the General Assembly sets the state school funding formula in the state budget [15], and voucher (Choice Scholarship) eligibility is set by state law [16].
recent_changes: 2025: Senate Enrolled Act 287 allowed school board candidates to declare a party affiliation; the Indiana School Boards Association opposed the change, and a supporter quoted by WNDU, a Noblesville school board member, said it adds transparency [17].

2026: Candidates choose a party, 'Independent' or no affiliation on their nominating petition, and that choice appears on the ballot; a candidate claiming the Democratic or Republican party must have voted in that party's primary in the two most recent primaries they voted in, or have certification from the county party chair, or can be challenged and removed from the ballot [2].

July 2026: Chalkbeat reported, citing Indiana School Boards Association data, that 524 of 1,044 candidates chose a party, about 72% of them Republicans [18]; the Indiana Election Division's 2026 guidance and the wording of the law differ on the primary-voting test, a question county election boards decide [19].

February 2026: Senate Enrolled Act 25 set the order of school board candidates on the ballot, grouped by party, with candidates who list no affiliation placed after the party and independent candidates [20].

2025: Senate Enrolled Act 1, a property tax law, limits how much operating revenue districts can raise through taxes and restricts school referendums to statewide general elections in even-numbered years [21, 22].
2025: The same law requires districts to share operating revenue with brick-and-mortar charter schools that enroll their students, statewide starting in 2028 [21, 22].
2025: The state budget opened Choice Scholarship vouchers to all Indiana families starting in June 2026 [16].
2026: The Indianapolis Public Education Corporation, rather than the Indianapolis Public Schools board, now certifies Indianapolis Public Schools referendum questions for the ballot [20].

2023: Senate Enrolled Act 391 changed the so-called $1 law so the Indiana Department of Education can order districts that lost at least 10% of enrollment over five years to close schools under 60% capacity and offer them to charter schools [23].
2023: House Enrolled Act 1447 required school districts to set up procedures for complaints that library material is obscene or harmful to minors [10].

race_context: The 'Huntington County Community School Board' races on the state list are for the Huntington County Community School Corporation (HCCS), based in Huntington [6, 24]. The district lists six elementary schools (Andrews, Flint Springs, Horace Mann, Lincoln, Roanoke and Salamonie), two middle schools (Crestview and Riverview), Huntington North High School and the Huntington North Learning Center [25]. Its 2027 budget workshop estimates enrollment (ADM) at 4,674 students [26].

The superintendent is Chuck Brimbury [27]. The Plain Dealer reported that superintendent John D. Trout resigned near the end of November 2025 [28]. The board named Brimbury interim superintendent, and on March 23, 2026 it voted 6-1 to make him permanent superintendent [28, 27]. Kenneth Thompson cast the no vote [29].

The board has seven members, each elected from one of seven districts by voters of that district, for four-year terms [24, 30]. Districts 2, 3 and 5 are on the 2026 ballot, and the other four seats were elected in 2024 [30, 31]. The 2026 officers are President Tim Allen (District 4), Vice President Ryan Wall (District 7) and Secretary Gary McClellan (District 5) [24, 32]. The other members are Matt Melcher (District 1), Debra Miller (District 2), Kenneth Thompson (District 3) and Aaron Carl (District 6) [33].

District 2 (one seat): Debra (Deb) Miller was appointed in January 2025 to fill the rest of Matthew Roth's term, after Roth resigned in December 2024 [34]. She is running unopposed and is listed as a Republican [6].

District 3 (one seat): Kari Heim was elected in 2022 and served from 2023 to 2025 [30, 35]. Kenneth Thompson held the seat and was voting by the Dec. 15, 2025 meeting [35]. He is running as Ken Thompson (Republican), against Carrie M Miller (Republican) and James Garwood (Independent) [6]. The state list's 'vote for 1' matches a single-member district [24].
District 5 (one seat): Gary McClellan held the seat in 2024 [30] and still does [33]. He is running unopposed and is listed as Nonpartisan [6].

Building projects and bonds (2025-2026): an Aug. 24, 2026 update listed work paid for by bonds issued in 2022 through 2025. The list includes Huntington North High School mechanical systems, locker rooms, restrooms and windows; Salamonie HVAC; secure vestibules at several elementary schools; and Horace Mann HVAC and Salamonie pool demolition scheduled for summer 2027 [36]. On Aug. 10, 2026, the board voted 7-0 for the project resolution on a 'tax neutral 2026 General Obligations Bond' [37]. It approved the final bond resolution and additional appropriation on Sept. 14 [38].

2027 budget (September-October 2026): CFO Michelle Babcock's workshop estimated a 2027 budget of $74.7 million across the debt service, education and operations funds [26]. The budget hearing was held on Sept. 28, 2026 [39]. Adoption of the budget, the 2027-2029 capital projects plan and a transfer from the Education Fund to the Operations Fund were on the Oct. 12, 2026 agenda [40]. HCCS is not on the state's list of districts with a referendum in November 2026 [41].

Academics and policy (2026): in March 2026 the board voted 7-0 to adopt a new K-12 science curriculum [28]. A May 11, 2026 work session covered the new state wireless-device law and the school accountability model [42].
Forums: this guide found no 2026 candidate forum, questionnaire or news profile for these races. The only contested race is District 3, with three candidates [6, 43].

candidates.summary: Incumbent by appointment, running unopposed; a retired Huntington County educator who joined the board in January 2025 [34, 6].
background: Told the board in her January 2025 interview that she had taught elementary, kindergarten and special education in Huntington County schools, had worked as a school counselor, and had been a building principal for 14 years, 10 of them in Huntington County [34].
Later worked for Pearson Education as an assessment specialist, and served as president of the YMCA Huntington Board, The Plain Dealer reported [34].
path_to_ballot: Was chosen by the board on a 4-2 vote on Jan. 14, 2025, out of six interviewed applicants, to fill the vacant District 2 seat [34].
Filed with a Republican affiliation; The Indiana Citizen's copy of the state list gives June 11, 2026 as her filing date [43, 6].

items: Said in her 2025 interview that one of her priorities is to 'attract and retain quality teachers' [34].
Said her goals are to encourage creative approaches to teaching and learning and that educators should look for research-based practices, The Plain Dealer reported [34].
Said she favors different ways of getting information to the community, noting that Huntington County 'no longer has a daily newspaper', The Plain Dealer reported [34].

on_incumbent: Voted for Brimbury's appointment as superintendent on March 23, 2026 [29]. At the Aug. 10, 2026 meeting she 'highlighted the positivity around tonights board meeting', according to the minutes [37].
gaps: No 2026 interview, questionnaire or campaign website was found.
No statement from her on SEA 1, the district budget or the 2026 bond was found.
No campaign finance reports were found.

candidates.summary: A Republican challenger for the District 3 seat held by Ken Thompson [6, 33].
path_to_ballot: Filed with a Republican affiliation; The Indiana Citizen's copy of the state list gives June 4, 2026 as her filing date [43, 6].
gaps: No news coverage, candidate statement, website or social media page was found for this candidate.
Occupation, community roles and ties to the schools are unknown.
No campaign finance reports were found.

candidates.summary: An Independent challenger for the District 3 seat held by Ken Thompson [6, 33].
path_to_ballot: Filed as an Independent; The Indiana Citizen's copy of the state list gives May 19, 2026 as his filing date [43, 6].
gaps: No news coverage, candidate statement, website or social media page was found for this candidate.
Occupation, community roles and ties to the schools are unknown.

candidates.summary: Incumbent: has held the District 3 seat since late 2025 and is running as a Republican [35, 6].
background: In April 2026 the board appointed him to the Warren Redevelopment Commission and Warren Park Board; he abstained on that vote [44].
path_to_ballot: Was voting as the District 3 member by the Dec. 15, 2025 meeting, when the board honored his predecessor, Kari Heim, for her 2023-25 service [35].
Filed with a Republican affiliation; The Indiana Citizen's copy of the state list gives June 5, 2026 as his filing date [43, 6].
on_incumbent: Cast the only no vote on March 23, 2026, when the board voted 6-1 to appoint Chuck Brimbury superintendent [29, 28].
Voted for the Aug. 10, 2026 resolutions on the 2026 general obligation bond, which passed 7-0 [37].
gaps: How and when he joined the board (likely an appointment to fill the vacancy left by Kari Heim) was not confirmed in a source read; search snippets mention public interviews for a vacant District 3 seat on Nov. 24, 2025, unverified.
No public explanation of his vote against the superintendent appointment was found.
Occupation and background not found in sources read; no campaign statement, website or finance report found.

candidates.summary: Incumbent and board secretary, running unopposed in District 5 [24, 6].
path_to_ballot: Held the District 5 seat in 2024, when The Plain Dealer listed it among the seats up in 2026 [30].
Filed for reelection; The Indiana Citizen's copy of the state list gives June 5, 2026 as his filing date [43]. The state lists him as Nonpartisan [6].
on_incumbent: On March 23, 2026, he seconded the motion to appoint Brimbury superintendent [29]. On Aug. 10, 2026, he seconded the motion on the 2026 general obligation bond project resolution, which passed 7-0 [37].
gaps: When he first joined the board was not confirmed.
No 2026 interview, questionnaire, campaign website or public statement on district issues was found.
Occupation not found in sources read; no campaign finance reports found.
